items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: but I had the basics under my finger, being taught by this teacher, Howard Shaw.

ctx.x: with my grandmother, and he didn't have the patience with me, so they sent me to a teacher.

Well, I was taught all the rudiments -- but I never really exerted myself to the point of studying like one would today. I was taught all the proper rudiments, but never practiced that much; I didn't have the interest to practice. I would take what was taught to me like the Bower system, and I wouldn't put the time and effort into it that somebody should today. This came later when I found out what I needed, but I had the basics under my finger, being taught by this teacher, Howard Shaw.

He taught me -- I knew a little bit of the keyboard, so the xylophone was in the book, too, so they taught me the xylophone, and I got into practicing at home, but I lost interest in that, too, because of the upper registers of the violin key notes, you know, and I didn't put enough time in, and I was out all the time. But I did like popular music, which was coming along about 1928 or '29, like showboat songs and so on and so forth, and so I would buy sheet music and apply it to the four mallets of the xylophone.
